name: overnight_gap_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Small-to-medium gaps (0.3%-1.0%) in Nifty50 stocks tend to fill within the first 90 minutes of trading. This happens because overnight gap pricing is driven by thin pre-market participation and global cue overreaction. Institutional traders who missed the overnight move provide liquidity in the opposite direction once the continuous session opens with full depth. Gaps > 1% are often news-driven and don't fill. This edge persists because gap-fill strategies require fast intraday execution that most retail traders can't implement systematically.

indicators.name: gap_filled
indicators.formula: close has touched prev_day_close since open

indicators.name: atr_20_daily
indicators.formula: ATR(high, low, close, 20) on daily bars

long.confirmation: first green bar (close > open) after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: first red bar (close < open) after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

exit.stop_loss: 0.5% beyond the gap direction (i.e., gap extension stop)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 50% of gap is filled

filters.volume_filter: opening 5-min volume > 80% of 20-day avg opening 5-min volume
filters.trend_filter: index gap must be < |0.5%| (don't fight macro gaps)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy, expiry day, result day for stock
other_filters: skip if gap > 1% — likely news-driven, won't fill

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural; pre-market pricing mechanics are unlikely to change

weaknesses: Opening 5 minutes have wide spreads and volatile prices — slippage can be 5+ bps
News-driven gaps masquerading as 'small gaps' will not fill — event filter helps but isn't foolproof
Low trade frequency (0-2 per day) means long stretches with no signals, testing patience
prior_art: Classic gap fill strategy — documented in Connors/Alvarez and others. NSE-specific adaptation.
notes: Backtest gap fill rates by gap size bucket (0.3-0.5%, 0.5-0.7%, 0.7-1.0%) to optimize thresholds.
